test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following chronological order of events of the freedom struggle is correct?

options.text: Non cooperative movement – Sepoy mutiny – Champaran movement – Partition of Bengal
Sepoy mutiny - Partition of Bengal - Champaran movement - Non cooperative movement
Non cooperative movement - Champaran movement - Partition of Bengal - Sepoy mutiny
Non cooperative movement - Champaran movement - Sepoy mutiny - Partition of Bengal

solution:
1905..The correct answer is __**Sepoy mutiny - Partition of Bengal - Champaran movement - Non cooperative movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The following chronological order of events of the freedom struggle is correct : **Sepoy mutiny - Partition of Bengal - Champaran movement - Non cooperative movement **.
 
• Indian Mutiny, also called Sepoy Mutiny or First War of Independence, widespread but unsuccessful rebellion against British rule in India in** 1857–59**. 
 
• The partition of Bengal took place in the year **1905**. It was a territorial reorganization of the Bengal Presidency implemented by the authorities of the British Raj.
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha of **1917** was the first Satyagraha movement led by Gandhi in India and is considered a historically important revolt in the Indian Independence Movement. 
 
• Noncooperation movement, unsuccessful attempt in** 1920–22**, organized by Mahatma Gandhi, to induce the British government of India to grant self-government, or swaraj, to India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Modern Indian History is considered the history **1850** onwards.
 
• A major part of Modern Indian History was occupied by the **British Rule in India**.
 
• Modern history is the history of the world beginning after the **Middle Ages**.
 
• Generally the term "**modern history**" refers to the history of the world since the advent of the Age of Reason and the Age of Enlightenment in the 17th and 18th centuries and the beginning of the Industrial Revolution.
